clue.text: Leading lady's crime

parts.note: read 'leading' as taking a bride to the altar: the offence is leading a second lady there while still married to the first

explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading lady' looks like the star of a play; here a man leads a lady up the aisle once too often.
explanation.definitionFit: Marrying while already wed to someone else is a criminal offence, the one committed by a husband leading a further lady to the altar.

clue.text: Flora's young man carrying towel

definitions.note: the possessive reads as the study of plants belonging to a flora

indicators.note: carrying says the young man holds the other piece inside him

parts.note: a boy is a young man
to towel someone is slang for to beat them, as is to tan

explanation.surface: Flora's boyfriend is holding a bath towel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'towel' looks like a bathroom item; as a verb it means to thrash, like tan.
explanation.definitionFit: Botany is the scientific study of plants, a region's flora.

clue.text: Dog running amok in tea garden

indicators.note: running amok means rampaging wildly, so the letters scatter into a new order

explanation.surface: A hound is rampaging through a café garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Dane is a giant breed of dog.

clue.text: Notes and letters from abroad I start to cumulate

parts.note: mu is a Greek letter; mus is its plural

indicators.note: start to picks the first letter of cumulate

explanation.surface: Someone abroad writes notes and letters they are beginning to pile up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters from abroad' are Greek letters, MUS; 'start to' takes C from 'cumulate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes collectively make up a melody or composition.

clue.text: Careless mistakes by carrier

parts.note: slips are small mistakes
a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: Someone sloppy keeps making errors, all blamed on the delivery firm.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod work is slovenly, done without proper care.

clue.text: Poetic performance from player since ignoring the odds

indicators.note: ignoring the odds means skipping the odd-numbered letters, keeping only the even ones

explanation.surface: A verse recital given by an actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A lyric is a short poem expressing personal feeling, often sung.

clue.text: Doctor's assistant Eugene and Edward put in picture, briefly

indicators.note: put in says the named pair goes inside the shortened picture
briefly says the picture word is cut short

parts.note: pic is short for picture
Eugene Aram was a notorious murderer, subject of a Thomas Hood poem
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A medic's aide named Eugene and his friend Edward pose for a snapshot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' shortens PICT(URE) to PIC, and 'put in' places ARAMED inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramedic is a trained ambulance worker giving emergency care, assisting doctors.

clue.text: Beautiful woman appearing on current occasion

indicators.note: in a down clue, appearing on means sitting above the next piece

parts.note: an hour is a particular time or occasion
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A lovely woman turns up at the present moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A houri is one of the beautiful maidens of the Islamic paradise.

clue.text: Set off from college in time

indicators.note: in says the college sits inside the time word

parts.note: a date is a point in time
Eton College is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone leaves college in good time.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to make it explode.

clue.text: It's likely one's inside? Right

parts.note: someone who is probably inside, as in jail, the 'Right' confirming the guess

explanation.definitionFit: A jailed convict is held inside, behind bars.

clue.text: Financial manager, having to negotiate endlessly with money lender, losing head

indicators.note: endlessly says the word for negotiate loses its final letter

parts.note: to treat is to negotiate terms

indicators.note: losing head says the lender's word drops its first letter

parts.note: a usurer lends money at interest

explanation.surface: A finance officer has to haggle with a loan shark and loses his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TREAT to TREA; 'losing head' cuts USURER to SURER.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer is the officer in charge of an organisation's funds.

clue.text: To depose king initially creates stir

indicators.note: initially says the king's letter is placed at the front, before the other piece

parts.note: R is short for Rex, Latin for king
to oust is to depose

explanation.surface: Overthrowing the monarch first of all causes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to rouse or stir someone up.

clue.text: Spots group of soldiers retreating when it's taken over

indicators.note: the word it, turned over, means the pair of letters spelling it are flipped round
retreating says the soldiers' word is read backwards, going the other way

parts.note: a section is a small unit of soldiers

explanation.surface: A platoon sees something while withdrawing as the enemy seize ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns SECTION into NOITCES; then 'it's taken over' flips the IT in it to TI.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot something is to notice it, so spots means sees.

clue.text: Detective's bloomer

definitions.meaning: Albert ... is the gentleman detective in Margery Allingham's novels
a bloomer is something that blooms: here a wild flower, red or white

explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake; it is a flower, a pink-like wildflower of hedgerows.
explanation.definitionFit: The detective bears the same name as a common wild flower of the pink family.

clue.text: Don't be offended-advice to curate at breakfast?

definitions.meaning: accept a remark without taking offence
the curate's egg, famously 'good in parts', from a Punch cartoon of a meek curate served a bad egg

explanation.walkthrough: In the Punch cartoon a curate, given a stale egg by his bishop, says it is good in parts.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something in good part is to receive it without resentment.

clue.text: Site meant for redevelopment as a cafe

indicators.note: a site redeveloped is rebuilt, so its letters are rebuilt in a different order

explanation.surface: Ground set aside for rebuilding is to become a coffee shop.
explanation.definitionFit: An estaminet is a small French bar or café.

clue.text: False teeth are readily available

parts.note: dentures sit on a dental plate, and the same phrase means handed over with no effort

explanation.definitionFit: Something handed to you with no effort is given freely, served up ready.

clue.text: What translates into "tapas"?

indicators.note: translates suggests rendering into another language, so the letters of the next words are rearranged

explanation.surface: What is the Italian for the Spanish bar snacks?
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of INTO + TAPAS is the Italian word for starters, which is just what tapas are.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasto is the Italian course of small appetisers, the counterpart of Spanish tapas.

clue.text: Persistent objections raised to 50% of boys joining navy

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means read upwards, reversing the objections

parts.note: buts are objections, as in 'no ifs or buts'

indicators.note: 50% of takes the first half of boys

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Determined protests go up as half the lads sign on as sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses BUTS to STUB; '50% of' takes BO from 'boys'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn means obstinately persistent, refusing to give way.

clue.text: Here tiny cattle roam-so we hear

indicators.note: the cattle wander about, so the letters of the words before move freely into a new order

explanation.surface: Somewhere hereabouts, small cows wander loose, or so the rumour goes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on 'roam', which sounds like Rome: 'roam, so we hear' is Rome, nicknamed the Eternal City. The setter makes 'roam' work twice.
explanation.definitionFit: Rome is traditionally called the Eternal City, and the clue's wandering word sounds just like that city's name.

clue.text: The purpose of camping

definitions.meaning: sleeping under canvas, in a tent

explanation.definitionFit: Intent is purpose or aim, and split in two it says sleeping under canvas.

clue.text: It's a mistake entrusting money to Australian bounder

indicators.note: entrusting money to the bounder means the money goes into his keeping, inside his word

parts.note: a boomer is a large male kangaroo, a bounder in Australia
L stands for libra, the pound sterling

explanation.surface: Lending cash to a cad from Down Under is an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounder' suggests a cad; it is a kangaroo, which bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a blunder, a silly error.

clue.text: One's employed in a pub to sell one short

definitions.text: One's employed in a pub to sell one short

parts.words: One's employed in a pub to sell one short
parts.note: 'sell one short' looks like cheating; a short is a measure of spirits, dispensed by a device fixed to an upturned bottle

explanation.walkthrough: A 'short' is a small measure of spirits, as against a long drink.
explanation.definitionFit: An optic is the bar device that measures out exact tots of spirits.

clue.text: Some clearer announcers broadcast again

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Presenters with clearer diction were put back on air.
explanation.definitionFit: Reran means repeated a programme, showed it a second time.

clue.text: Clever use of ball steals set back

indicators.note: set back says the whole run so far is read in reverse

parts.note: to nip is slang for to steal
to gel is to set, like a jelly

explanation.surface: A thief pinches things and puts them back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses NIPS+GEL to give LEG+SPIN. Leg-spin is a cricket bowling style where the ball turns from the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg-spin is a crafty cricket bowling technique, wrist-spinning the delivery to deceive the batsman.

clue.text: Saw international banker

definitions.meaning: the '... of Zurich' was a nickname for Swiss financiers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like a tool; it is an old saying.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnome is a pithy maxim, and Swiss bankers were mocked as the gnomes of Zurich.

clue.text: Frequently front of cushion comes off

indicators.note: front of picks out the first letter of the cushioning word as the one to go
comes off says that first letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to cushion a blow is to soften it

explanation.surface: Often the front of a pillow comes away.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means many times, at frequent intervals.

clue.text: Lost trousers have finally turned up

indicators.note: lost suggests the garment is all at sea, so its letters are rearranged
finally picks the last letter of the word have

explanation.surface: Missing trousers have at last been found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' rearranges TROUSERS to RETROUSS; 'finally' adds E from 'have'.
explanation.definitionFit: Retroussé describes a nose tilted upward at the tip, a French borrowing.

clue.text: Poison inside pleasing round container

indicators.note: inside says the round container sits within the pleasing word

parts.note: nice means pleasing
O is round in shape
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: Something toxic is hidden in an attractive circular box.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicotine, the alkaloid in tobacco, is toxic in sufficient doses.

clue.text: Rebuffed admirer's temperature beginning to rise

indicators.note: rebuffed means pushed back, so the admirer's word is read backwards

parts.note: a lover is an admirer

indicators.note: beginning picks the first letter of temperature

explanation.surface: A rejected suitor feels his temperature start to climb.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolt is to rise up against authority.
